nodes.norm_label: d-012 request variant with a free apply() function
nodes.rationale: Request is std::variant<NewOrder, Cancel, Modify> with a free apply(book, request, out), so fuzz, replay, bench and the exchange all feed the same stream type.

nodes.rationale: Moved unchanged from sim_noise_trader_test.cpp so the informed-trader tests share it; Integration.FiveMinutesOfTheDefaultNoiseFlow then expected 11 agents, and the default config's event hash changed while a config with no informed section keeps the noise-only hash ac6dbb79a513fa50.

nodes.label: Quantity Conservation Invariant
nodes.rationale: For every order, filled + cancelled + resting = accepted qty, adjusted by the change in remaining qty at each modify; checked in tests.

nodes.label: Timer Overhead Measurement
nodes.rationale: The timer's own overhead is measured and reported; if it is significant, batches are timed instead of single messages.

nodes.label: D-074 orders.log plain-text codec
nodes.rationale: Decimal integers only (enums and bools as their integer values), written and read through one codec (format_request/parse_request, format_header/parse_header); the replay tool and the replay test use the same functions, and the test replays the parsed text rather than retained Request objects.

nodes.label: micro_bench Google Benchmark target
nodes.rationale: Microbenchmarks of the lob library linked with benchmark::benchmark_main.

nodes.label: Microbenchmarks (Google Benchmark, 1k and 100k-order books)
nodes.rationale: Add non-crossing, cancel, aggressive order matching one level, modify-reduce and best-price query, with the book pre-filled to 1k and 100k orders.

nodes.label: D-011 Event variant appended to a caller-owned vector
nodes.norm_label: d-011 event variant appended to a caller-owned vector
nodes.rationale: Event is std::variant<Ack, Reject, Trade, Cancelled, Modified> appended to a caller-owned std::vector<Event>: the alternatives are trivially copyable and nothing allocates once the buffer has grown (SPEC 3.7).

nodes.label: D-060 Benchmark order lifetimes counted in new-order arrivals
nodes.norm_label: d-060 benchmark order lifetimes counted in new-order arrivals
nodes.rationale: The bench has no clock; exponential lifetimes with a mean of 1,500 arrivals hold the book near 1,000 resting orders, like the simulator's noise flow.

nodes.label: D-061 lobsim_bench three timed passes: block, batch, message
nodes.norm_label: d-061 lobsim_bench three timed passes: block, batch, message
nodes.rationale: The clock advances in 41 ns steps and a message takes about 21 ns, so single-message samples cannot resolve the body of the distribution (SPEC 7: 'time batches if it's significant'): blocks of 4,096 messages give throughput, batches of 32 the body, and per-message timing the far tail and maximum.

nodes.label: D-062 Allocation counter on only during engine calls
nodes.norm_label: d-062 allocation counter on only during engine calls
nodes.rationale: With the caller's event buffer reserved once, every counted allocation is the engine's own.

nodes.label: D-063 Microbenchmarks time batches of 128 operations
nodes.norm_label: d-063 microbenchmarks time batches of 128 operations
nodes.rationale: Pausing the timer per operation costs more than the operation, and each batch is undone outside the timed region so the book stays near its nominal size.

nodes.label: D-065 micro_bench timer-overhead calibration benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Two calibration benchmarks run an empty operation in batches of 128, with and without one timer pause per batch; the difference is the timer overhead included in the per-operation times of the five pausing benchmarks, and the README reports it instead of an estimate.

nodes.label: Limit FOK order
nodes.rationale: A read-only dry run in priority order counts fillable quantity; if short, Ack then Cancelled(FOKUnfillable) and nothing else changes.

nodes.label: lob (matching engine library)
nodes.rationale: lob does not depend on sim; holds types and events, ObjectPool, OrderBook, ReferenceBook and apply().

nodes.label: Integer ticks and lots
nodes.rationale: Prices are int64 ticks and quantities int64 lots, decimals only for display: no floating-point equality bugs in matching.

nodes.label: Self-trade prevention (CancelTaking / CancelResting)
nodes.rationale: The taker's mode decides: CancelTaking (default) cancels the taker remainder with Cancelled(SelfTrade); CancelResting cancels the resting order and keeps matching.

nodes.label: Request validation check order
nodes.rationale: Runs before any state change and the first failing check wins, so both books report the same reason; a rejected request changes nothing and consumes no order id.

nodes.label: Array-indexed price ladder (stretch goal)
nodes.rationale: Would remove the O(log L) std::map lookup when adding to an existing level.

nodes.label: lobsim
nodes.rationale: Limit order book, matching engine and agent-based trading simulator in C++20; same config and seed give byte-identical output files.

nodes.label: Modelling scope limits (what is not modelled)
nodes.norm_label: modelling scope limits (what is not modelled)
nodes.rationale: One instrument, no networking or FIX, single-threaded, no auctions, no stop/iceberg/hidden orders, no decrement-and-cancel STP, no real market data, non-adaptive agents, fees only in MM accounting.

nodes.label: DECISIONS.md (decision log)
nodes.rationale: Records every decision the specification left open, one line each with the reason.

nodes.label: Noise-trader symmetric reference price (D-088 to D-090)
nodes.norm_label: noise-trader symmetric reference price (d-088 to d-090)
nodes.rationale: The spec rule floor(mid) -/+ d puts sells one tick closer to the mid with an odd spread, so the price falls about 106 ticks an hour with no information; default config uses symmetric (buy ceil(mid) - d, sell floor(mid) + d); the spec rule stays the default when the key is absent.

nodes.label: std::map price levels
nodes.rationale: Required by the specification; adding to an existing level is O(log L), only the best level is O(1); each new level costs one 80-byte map node allocation.

nodes.label: AvellanedaStoikovMM
nodes.rationale: One post-only bid and ask of 5 lots recomputed on every BBO, every private message and every 100 ms; no bid at inventory 50 or more, no ask at -50 or less; gamma 0.0001, kappa 1.5, 50 us latency.

nodes.label: Market-maker stress test
nodes.rationale: Aggressive test agent, small inventory limit and heavy jitter; an outside observer checks the pending-request rule, at most one resting order per side, the inventory bound and that beliefs equal exchange state; every race path occurs hundreds of times over six seeds.

nodes.label: Avellaneda-Stoikov model
nodes.rationale: Reservation price r = s - q*gamma*sigma^2*(T-t), total spread gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) + (2/gamma)*ln(1 + gamma/kappa); the inventory penalty shrinks toward the session end, so inventory control fades.

nodes.label: Engine events (Ack, Reject, Trade, Cancelled, Modified)
nodes.norm_label: engine events (ack, reject, trade, cancelled, modified)
nodes.rationale: Appended to a caller-owned buffer in the order they happen.

nodes.label: Market-maker repricing near inventory limit (D-092)
nodes.rationale: A modify sets remaining quantity, so a late modify could refill after unseen fills and push inventory to q_max + 2*quote_size - 2; reprice by modify only when a full extra quote cannot break the limit, else cancel then new order, bounding inventory by q_max + quote_size - 1.

nodes.label: Modify priority rules
nodes.rationale: Same price with smaller quantity reduces in place and keeps queue position; a price change or quantity increase re-enters as a new arrival with the same id; new_qty is the new remaining quantity; Modified is emitted before any trade it causes.

nodes.label: Market-maker pending-request rule
nodes.rationale: Never sends a request for one side while an earlier one on that side is unanswered; every request has exactly one reply and fills are not replies; an UnknownOrder reject means the order was already filled.

nodes.label: Outward quote rounding on the tick grid
nodes.norm_label: outward quote rounding on the tick grid
nodes.rationale: Quotes are floor(r - delta/2) and ceil(r + delta/2), giving 2- or 3-tick quotes; with non-zero inventory this yields a mean 2.70-tick quote against the market's 1.94.

nodes.label: lobsim_replay
nodes.rationale: Replays orders.log into a fresh lob::OrderBook and prints the engine event hash, which equals engine_event_hash in summary.json.

nodes.label: lobsim_run
nodes.rationale: Runs a simulation from a config (--seed, --duration-s overrides) and writes orders.log, trades.csv, bbo.csv, mm_fills.csv and summary.json.

nodes.label: Sample run (default config, seed 42)
nodes.rationale: One simulated hour: 331,640 requests, 51,653 trades, 158,982 lots, engine event hash 5aa4b082b3f2168c, 0.3 s wall clock; market maker PnL +12,263 ticks.

nodes.label: Engine event hash (FNV-1a 64-bit)
nodes.rationale: FNV-1a over a fixed little-endian encoding of every field of every event; equality of hashes proves replay and differential equivalence.

nodes.norm_label: d-002 cmakepresets.json: debug, release and sanitize presets

nodes.norm_label: d-004 third-party targets system, benchmark_enable_werror off

nodes.norm_label: d-006 lobsim_werror adds -werror to own targets

nodes.norm_label: d-007 build type defaults to release
nodes.rationale: With no CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE, a bare cmake -S . -B build should give the fast binaries the benchmarks describe.

nodes.label: D-049 Default fuzz mode as 10 ctest entries of 20 seeds
nodes.norm_label: d-049 default fuzz mode as 10 ctest entries of 20 seeds
nodes.rationale: The sanitize build takes several minutes serially, so the test presets run the entries as 10 jobs.

nodes.label: D-078 -ffp-contract=off is PUBLIC on the sim target
nodes.norm_label: d-078 -ffp-contract=off is public on the sim target
nodes.rationale: The generators and the fundamental step are inline in headers and compiled into every user of them, so the flag must reach them too; fused multiply-adds would make floating-point results depend on the build type.

nodes.label: D-100 All metrics from one passive MetricsObserver
nodes.norm_label: d-100 all metrics from one passive metricsobserver
nodes.rationale: It sees engine events and the true top of book with zero latency but never schedules, sends or draws, and a test checks that attaching it leaves the event hash and orders.log unchanged; lobsim_run no longer has its own market-maker probe and prints only what the agent alone knows (requests, rejects, anomalies, believed inventory).

nodes.label: D-109 Output file formats for CSVs and summary.json
nodes.norm_label: d-109 output file formats for csvs and summary.json
nodes.rationale: CSV files write integers as integers, sides as buy/sell, roles as maker/taker, mid and markouts with %.1f (multiples of 0.5), fundamental and PnL with %.6f, and an undefined value as an empty field; summary.json uses nlohmann::ordered_json (key order fixed in code, config echoed from to_json), doubles through %.6f and null when undefined (return mean and sd use %.6e because they are around 1e-6), two-space indent and a trailing newline. No wall-clock time, host name or path is written; elapsed time goes to stdout only.

nodes.label: D-110 replay_log is the one replay implementation
nodes.norm_label: d-110 replay_log is the one replay implementation
nodes.rationale: It lives in the sim library and lobsim_replay, tests/replay.cpp and the command-line test all use it; a bad header or request line throws ReplayError carrying the 1-based line number, which the tool prints before exiting 1. cli_run_then_replay runs lobsim_run --duration-s 120, replays the log, compares the printed hash with summary.json and checks that a corrupted log is refused.

nodes.label: Zero-warnings policy (SPEC Section 8)
nodes.rationale: 'Zero warnings' applies to the project's own code and is enforced by every build through -Werror instead of by reading logs; pinned third-party targets are exempt so a newer compiler cannot break them.

nodes.label: D-025 Same-price larger-qty modify moves order to level tail
nodes.norm_label: d-025 same-price larger-qty modify moves order to level tail
nodes.rationale: priority_kept = false; the order cannot match because the book is never crossed.

nodes.label: D-028 Cancelled.qty_cancelled and Trade.aggressor_side meanings
nodes.rationale: qty_cancelled is the order's remaining quantity at that moment; aggressor_side is the taker's side.

nodes.label: D-026 Modified.new_qty is the requested qty before re-entry matching
nodes.norm_label: d-026 modified.new_qty is the requested qty before re-entry matching
nodes.rationale: The Modified event is emitted first (SPEC 3.3.6), before any matching the re-entry causes.

nodes.label: Determinism and replay tests
nodes.rationale: Tests compare runs with each other instead of pinning a fixed hash, because the hash can differ across platforms' maths libraries.

nodes.label: Deterministic byte-identical output
nodes.rationale: Same config and seed give byte-identical files; bit-identical for the same build and platform, but libm log, sin and cos may differ in the last bit across platforms, so no test pins a fixed simulation hash.

nodes.label: -ffp-contract=off
nodes.rationale: Compiled so that fused multiply-adds cannot change results between builds.

nodes.label: Observers (zero-latency, read-only)
nodes.rationale: Observers cannot schedule, send or draw random numbers, so attaching metrics never changes a run.

nodes.label: Per-agent RNG streams
nodes.rationale: Derived from the master seed and the agent's role and index, so adding an agent never changes another agent's draws; message-triggered draws (a noise trader's order lifetime on Ack) use a separate stream so latency jitter cannot re-phase the decision stream.

nodes.label: Sequence-number tie-break rule
nodes.rationale: Events with equal time are processed in scheduling order (global seq counter); event kind and agent id never take part, so simultaneous events have a documented order.

nodes.label: NoiseTrader (zero-intelligence Poisson trader)
nodes.rationale: Wakes as a Poisson process with rate lambda; picks a limit order with probability p_limit, otherwise a market order, side 50/50, size uniform in [1, max_size].

nodes.label: Zero-Intelligence (ZI) Order Flow
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the background market because it is simple, explainable and a known baseline: budget-constrained random traders reach near-100% allocative efficiency [15], and order flow can be modeled as Poisson streams of limit orders, market orders and cancellations [16]. The README must call ZI models known simplifications.

nodes.norm_label: daniels et al., a quantitative model of trading and price formation

nodes.label: Gode & Sunder (1993), Allocative Efficiency of Markets with Zero-Intelligence Traders
nodes.norm_label: gode & sunder (1993), allocative efficiency of markets with zero-intelligence traders

nodes.label: Smith, Farmer, Gillemot, Krishnamurthy: Statistical Theory of the Continuous Double Auction
nodes.norm_label: smith, farmer, gillemot, krishnamurthy: statistical theory of the continuous double auction

nodes.label: Default Config Sanity Check
nodes.rationale: At t=0, γσ²T = 0.36 ticks and (2/γ)ln(1+γ/κ) ≈ 1.33 ticks, so the total spread starts near 1.7 ticks and narrows to about 1.33; each lot shifts r by at most 0.36 ticks (a 5-lot fill about 1.8); noise flow of 50 wakeups/s gives about 42 limit orders/s and, with a 30 s mean lifetime, a steady book on the order of 1,000 orders.

nodes.label: Exponential Order Lifetime Cancellation
nodes.rationale: Each acked resting order draws an Exp(1/order_lifetime_mean_s) lifetime and a scheduled cancel, a constant cancel rate that lets the book reach a steady size instead of growing forever; UnknownOrder rejects for orders already filled are ignored.

nodes.label: D-020 UnknownOrder means not resting right now
nodes.norm_label: d-020 unknownorder means not resting right now
nodes.rationale: Never-assigned, fully filled and already-cancelled ids are indistinguishable to the caller, and the id index only knows resting orders.

nodes.label: D-044 Id index grows only on rest; validate() checks indexed_ count
nodes.norm_label: d-044 id index grows only on rest; validate() checks indexed_ count
nodes.rationale: Lookups bounds-check, so any id beyond the index is UnknownOrder. Comparing indexed_ (kept by the single writer set_index()) with the resting-order count avoids scanning the whole index, which grows with every id ever rested and would make a per-message validate() O(total ids); a pool live count == resting orders check catches a leaked node.

nodes.label: Mid vs fundamental chart (seed 42)
nodes.rationale: Line chart of price (ticks) against time (s) for the one-hour seed-42 sample run: blue = fundamental value, orange = exchange mid, grey band = warm-up. It shows how well the exchange price discovers the latent value. Both series start at 10000 ticks. The fundamental wanders between about 9934 and 10000 ticks, while the mid follows only its slow trend (down to about 9949 near 3070 s, then back up). The two meet again near 9965 ticks at about 3600 s.

nodes.label: Mid-fundamental gap (loose tracking)
nodes.rationale: What the chart shows: the blue fundamental is a rough random walk with swings of tens of ticks. The orange mid moves as a smooth, stepwise curve that follows only the slow trend, lagging by hundreds of seconds and never reaching the troughs. The widest visible gap is about 30 ticks near t=500 s (fundamental about 9954, mid about 9984). Near t=3000 s the fundamental is about 9935 and the mid about 9955. Why: only the informed trader reads the fundamental. At Poisson wake-ups it sends a small market IOC order when the value is at least theta ticks beyond the far touch, while noise traders anchor on the current mid. So the price is pulled toward the value only intermittently.

nodes.label: Self-Implemented RNG and Distributions
nodes.rationale: std:: distributions are implementation-defined and differ across standard libraries, so lobsim implements SplitMix64 seeding, xoshiro256** and its own distributions to keep results reproducible.

nodes.label: Determinism (same config + seed gives byte-identical outputs)
nodes.norm_label: determinism (same config + seed gives byte-identical outputs)
nodes.rationale: Reproducibility is a hard requirement: the simulation is single-threaded with int64 nanosecond time and no wall clock, unordered-container iteration order never affects results, ties are broken by sequence number and the RNG is self-implemented. Results are bit-identical per build and platform; across platforms libm log may differ in the last bit.

nodes.label: Per-Agent RNG Streams from One Master Seed
nodes.norm_label: per-agent rng streams from one master seed
nodes.rationale: Each agent's stream is derived from the master seed so adding an agent never changes the others' draws.

nodes.label: D-102 Market-maker cash, inventory, fees and marked PnL
nodes.norm_label: d-102 market-maker cash, inventory, fees and marked pnl
nodes.rationale: cash is int64 ticks x lots (a buy subtracts price * qty, a sell adds it) and inventory is in lots, both from t = 0; fees are doubles, qty * maker_fee_ticks as maker else qty * taker_fee_ticks (a negative fee is a rebate); pnl(t) = cash + inventory * mid(t) - fees with mid(t) the last defined mid at or before t, and a mark of 0 if no mid has ever existed.

nodes.label: lob_tests GoogleTest executable
nodes.rationale: Matching-engine unit tests linked against lob and GTest::gtest_main and registered with gtest_discover_tests.

nodes.label: Core Types (Price, Qty, OrderId, OwnerId, Side, OrderType, TIF, STP)
nodes.norm_label: core types (price, qty, orderid, ownerid, side, ordertype, tif, stp)
nodes.rationale: Price is int64 ticks in [1, max_price] and Qty int64 lots > 0; OrderId is assigned by the engine, starts at 1 and is strictly increasing; STP defaults to CancelTaking.

nodes.label: Differential Fuzz Test (OrderBook vs ReferenceBook)
nodes.rationale: A seeded generator emits valid and invalid requests (unknown ids, zero qty, crossing post-only, all order types, few owners so STP triggers); both books must produce identical event streams over at least 200 seeds x 10,000 messages, with a --long mode for 10^6+.

nodes.label: Engine Events (Ack, Reject, Trade, Cancelled, Modified)
nodes.norm_label: engine events (ack, reject, trade, cancelled, modified)
nodes.rationale: Appended to a caller-owned buffer so there is no allocation per call once it has grown; within a request they appear in the order they happen (Ack/Modified, then trades and STP cancels in match order, then any final Cancelled). trade_id starts at 1.

nodes.label: lob Library (matching engine)
nodes.rationale: Must not depend on the sim library, keeping the matching engine standalone.

nodes.label: Maker / Taker (trades execute at the maker's price)
nodes.norm_label: maker / taker (trades execute at the maker's price)

nodes.label: Market Orders (IOC only)
nodes.rationale: Match at any price and never rest; the remainder is cancelled (NoLiquidity if nothing filled, else IOCRemainder). Market orders must be IOC and their price is ignored by validation.

nodes.label: Matching Rules
nodes.rationale: Accepted orders are Acked with a fresh OrderId before any other event; a buy matches asks at or below its limit (best price first, FIFO within a level) with each fill at the maker's price; GTC remainder rests at the tail of its level and IOC/market remainder is cancelled; Cancel emits Cancelled(User).

nodes.label: Order Requests (NewOrder, Cancel, Modify)
nodes.rationale: Modify carries new_qty as the new remaining quantity.

nodes.label: Order Types and Time-in-Force (GTC, IOC, FOK, Market, Post-only)
nodes.norm_label: order types and time-in-force (gtc, ioc, fok, market, post-only)

nodes.label: Post-Only Orders
nodes.rationale: Guarantees maker status: a GTC limit is rejected with PostOnlyWouldCross if it would match on arrival (buy price >= best ask, or sell price <= best bid).

nodes.label: Hand-Checkable Unit Test Scenarios
nodes.rationale: Small scenarios covering the worked example, maker-price trades, multi-level sweeps, FIFO, IOC remainder, NoLiquidity, FOK exact and one-lot-short, post-only reject, modify priority rules, cancel errors, both STP modes including FOK dry runs, and level cleanup; every behaviour in Section 3 needs at least one test.

nodes.label: Worked Matching Example (buy 10 @ 101 vs asks A, B, C)
nodes.norm_label: worked matching example (buy 10 @ 101 vs asks a, b, c)
nodes.rationale: Hand-verifiable reference scenario: fills 5 vs A then 3 vs B at 101 (time priority), stops before C at 102 (above the limit) and rests 2 at 101; with a 105 limit the first fills still print at 101 (maker price). Reused as a unit test.

nodes.label: Cboe Futures Exchange BOEv3 Modify Order Specification
nodes.norm_label: cboe futures exchange boev3 modify order specification

nodes.label: Fill-or-Kill (FOK) Dry Run
nodes.rationale: A read-only dry run walks the book in priority order and sums fillable quantity before anything executes, so an unfillable FOK yields only Ack then Cancelled(FOKUnfillable) with no other side effects. STP applies to the dry run: a same-owner maker is skipped under CancelResting and ends the dry run under CancelTaking.

nodes.label: Modify Semantics (reduce in place keeps priority)
nodes.norm_label: modify semantics (reduce in place keeps priority)
nodes.rationale: Modify semantics must be explicit. Following Cboe [4], a same-price quantity reduction keeps time priority; a quantity increase or any price change loses it (removed and re-entered as a new arrival with the same OrderId, keeping post_only and stp, possibly trading as taker). Modified is emitted before any trades it causes; a post-only modify that would cross is rejected and the original order is unchanged.

nodes.label: Pending-Request Rule (one unanswered request per side)
nodes.norm_label: pending-request rule (one unanswered request per side)
nodes.rationale: Never send a new request for a side while a previous one on that side has no Ack/Modified/Cancelled/Reject yet; this prevents the classic stale-state bug. PostOnlyWouldCross and UnknownOrder rejects (e.g. a modify racing a fill) must be handled without crashing or desyncing.

nodes.label: Request Validation Order (first failing check wins)
nodes.norm_label: request validation order (first failing check wins)
nodes.rationale: Checks run before any state change in a fixed order (new orders: InvalidQty, InvalidFlags, InvalidPrice, PostOnlyWouldCross; cancels: UnknownOrder, NotOwner; modifies: UnknownOrder, NotOwner, InvalidQty, InvalidPrice, NoChange, PostOnlyWouldCross) so both books report the same reason; a rejected request changes nothing and assigns no OrderId.

nodes.label: Self-Trade Prevention (CancelTaking / CancelResting)
nodes.rationale: Agents can accidentally cross themselves, and exchanges offer cancel-newest and cancel-oldest STP modes [5]. The taker's mode decides: CancelTaking (default) cancels the taker's remainder and leaves the maker untouched; CancelResting cancels the maker and matching continues.

nodes.label: Agent Interface (on_start, on_wakeup, on_market_data, on_private)
nodes.rationale: ctx gives now(), send(request), schedule_wakeup(t) and an RNG; agents keep their own view of the book (last received BBO) and their own orders, and never read the exchange's book directly.

nodes.label: Event Queue (min-heap on (time_ns, seq))
nodes.rationale: Simulation time is int64 nanoseconds with no wall clock; seq is a global counter incremented on every schedule, so equal times are processed in scheduling order (documented in the README).

nodes.label: Exchange (wraps one OrderBook)
nodes.rationale: Processes each arriving request instantly, then sends private events to their owners after response_latency (a Trade to both maker and taker) and public market data to every subscriber after its feed_latency.

nodes.label: Latent Fundamental Value V
nodes.rationale: Gaussian random walk in ticks starting at initial_price: every dt_s, V += σ_f √Δt Z. Only the informed trader sees it.

nodes.label: InformedTrader
nodes.rationale: Wakes at Poisson rate lambda and market-buys size if V − ask >= θ or market-sells if bid − V >= θ, using its delayed local BBO; it is the source of adverse selection.

nodes.label: Per-Agent Latency Model (entry, response, feed)
nodes.rationale: entry: agent to exchange; response: exchange to owner (acks, fills, cancels); feed: exchange to agent (public market data). Each is a constant plus optional uniform jitter in [0, jitter], configured per agent.

nodes.label: lobsim_replay Tool
nodes.rationale: Feeds logged requests straight into a fresh OrderBook and prints the engine event-stream hash, which must equal the hash recorded by the live run.

nodes.label: Market Statistics (spread, excess kurtosis, return ACFs)
nodes.norm_label: market statistics (spread, excess kurtosis, return acfs)
nodes.rationale: Spread distribution, plus log returns of mids sampled every sample_interval_s: excess kurtosis, ACF of r_t at lags 1-5 and ACF of |r_t| at lags 1-10.

nodes.label: Metrics (after warm-up, on the exchange's true book)
nodes.norm_label: metrics (after warm-up, on the exchange's true book)
nodes.rationale: All statistics are measured after warmup_s using the exchange's true book as ground truth, not any agent's delayed view.

nodes.label: MM Accounting (mark-to-market PnL)
nodes.rationale: Cash in ticks x lots as int64, fees as double; reports fills, volume, final inventory, max |inventory|, PnL = cash + q x mid − fees, fraction of time quoting both sides and average quoted spread.

nodes.label: NoiseTrader Reference Price and Limit Placement
nodes.norm_label: noisetrader reference price and limit placement
nodes.rationale: ref = floor of the local BBO mid, else last trade, else initial_price; buys at ref − d and sells at ref + d with d uniform in [1, D], GTC. The delayed view means a limit order can occasionally cross the real book and trade, which is expected.

nodes.label: orders.log Request Log
nodes.rationale: Every request arriving at the exchange is appended with its time so the run can be replayed.

nodes.label: Run Output Files (trades.csv, bbo.csv, mm_fills.csv, summary.json, orders.log)
nodes.norm_label: run output files (trades.csv, bbo.csv, mm_fills.csv, summary.json, orders.log)
nodes.rationale: bbo.csv is sampled, mm_fills.csv carries markouts, and summary.json records all metrics plus config, seed and the engine event hash.

nodes.label: Public Market Data (BBO and TradePrint)
nodes.rationale: A BBO{bid, bid_qty, ask, ask_qty} message whenever top-of-book changes and a TradePrint{price, qty, aggressor_side} per trade.

nodes.label: Replay Test
nodes.rationale: The live-run engine event hash must equal the hash obtained by replaying orders.log.

nodes.label: Run Plots (tools/plot.py)
nodes.rationale: Optional pandas + matplotlib plots: mid vs fundamental, MM inventory, MM PnL, spread histogram and return ACF.

nodes.label: Stylized Facts (heavy tails, no return autocorrelation, volatility clustering)
nodes.norm_label: stylized facts (heavy tails, no return autocorrelation, volatility clustering)
nodes.rationale: Measured, never tuned for: the simulator must not be tuned to fake them, and the README must say honestly which appear and which do not.

nodes.norm_label: building a price-time-priority order book in c++

nodes.norm_label: byrd, hybinette, balch: abides, towards high-fidelity market simulation for ai research

nodes.label: Bit-Exact on Every Public Scenario and About 90x Faster (NeurIPS 2026)
nodes.norm_label: bit-exact on every public scenario and about 90x faster (neurips 2026)
nodes.rationale: Cited for reimplementers having to reverse-engineer ABIDES's undocumented ordering of simultaneous events.

nodes.norm_label: coletta et al., towards realistic market simulations: a gan approach

nodes.label: Cont (2001) Stylized Facts, via Ratliff-Crain et al., Revisiting Cont's Stylized Facts for Modern Stock Markets
nodes.norm_label: cont (2001) stylized facts, via ratliff-crain et al., revisiting cont's stylized facts for modern stock markets

nodes.label: Exact First, Then Fast: An Event-for-Event C++ Rebuild of the Agenthon ABIDES Market (NeurIPS 2026)
nodes.norm_label: exact first, then fast: an event-for-event c++ rebuild of the agenthon abides market (neurips 2026)
nodes.rationale: Cited for ABIDES's Python reference processing only about 14,000 events/s.

nodes.label: Discrete-Event Simulation (timestamped messages with latency)
nodes.rationale: ABIDES's message-based design, modeled on NASDAQ ITCH/OUCH with configurable pairwise latencies [6], shows message passing plus latency is the right architecture; every interaction is a timestamped message.

nodes.label: Engine Event Hash (FNV-1a 64-bit)
nodes.rationale: Hashing a fixed little-endian binary encoding of every field of every event gives a compact fingerprint of the engine event stream for the determinism and replay checks.

nodes.label: Explicit Sequence-Number Tie-Breaking
nodes.rationale: ABIDES's Python reference processes only about 14,000 events/s [7] and reimplementers had to reverse-engineer its undocumented ordering of simultaneous events [8]; a C++ core with ties broken by an explicit, documented sequence number keeps results reproducible, and determinism is tested.

nodes.label: Fills Only Through the Matching Engine (real queue position, delayed views)
nodes.norm_label: fills only through the matching engine (real queue position, delayed views)
nodes.rationale: Fills depend on queue position and on how stale the agent's view is; hftbacktest models feed latency, order latency and queue position, while bar-based backtests cannot simulate queue position [9]. Agents see the market only through delayed messages.

nodes.label: Integer Ticks and Lots (int64 prices and quantities)
nodes.norm_label: integer ticks and lots (int64 prices and quantities)
nodes.rationale: Floating-point prices cause equality and rounding bugs; production-style engines use int64 ticks/lots and convert decimals only at the boundary [2], and a teaching engine notes a real one would never use std::map<double, ...> [3]. Decimals are for display only.

nodes.label: Interactive Agent-Based Simulation (not historical replay)
nodes.rationale: Pure historical replay cannot simulate the market's response to the tested agent's own orders [10]; replay of lobsim's own logs is used only for determinism checks.

nodes.label: Per-Channel FIFO Delivery
nodes.rationale: arrival = max(sampled_arrival, last_arrival_on_channel), so jitter can never deliver a message before an earlier one on the same channel.

nodes.label: Metrics, output files, replay and plots (Phase 7; SPEC 5.7, 6, 9 item 7)
nodes.norm_label: metrics, output files, replay and plots (phase 7; spec 5.7, 6, 9 item 7)

nodes.label: D-106 Markout uses the mid in force at t + h
nodes.norm_label: d-106 markout uses the mid in force at t + h
nodes.rationale: The mid at t + h is the state after all events with timestamp <= t + h, resolved lazily when the next later event arrives or at the end; a sample is skipped and counted if the mid is undefined then or t + h > T (t + h == T is valid), so n + skipped equals the number of window fills. Statistics are the mean, sample sd (n - 1), 95% interval mean +- 1.96 sd / sqrt(n) (null for n < 2) and quantity-weighted mean; fills before the warm-up get markouts in mm_fills.csv but are not in the statistics.

nodes.label: D-112 mid_before: mid just before the fill's request
nodes.norm_label: d-112 mid_before: mid just before the fill's request
nodes.rationale: Captured in on_request; undefined when the book is one-sided at that moment, however recently a mid existed, and such a fill is left out of the decomposition just as the markout treats an undefined mid at t + h. It is the mid_before column of mm_fills.csv, placed before the markout_* columns.

nodes.label: D-113 spread_capture against the pre-trade mid
nodes.norm_label: d-113 spread_capture against the pre-trade mid
nodes.rationale: spread_capture = mid_before - p for a buy and p - mid_before for a sell (ticks per lot): what the fill earned against the pre-trade mid; the summary.json spread_capture block covers window fills with a defined mid_before (n, mean, sd, 95% interval, quantity-weighted mean).

nodes.label: D-114 mid_move(h): the adverse-selection component
nodes.rationale: mid_move(h) = m(t+h) - mid_before for a buy and mid_before - m(t+h) for a sell, with m(t+h) exactly as in the markout; negative means the price moved against the market maker. It is computed as markout(h) - spread_capture, so markout = spread_capture + mid_move holds on every fill where all three are defined.

nodes.label: D-115 Decomposition only over fills with mid_before defined
nodes.norm_label: d-115 decomposition only over fills with mid_before defined
nodes.rationale: Each markout's decomposition covers window fills whose markout and mid_before are both defined, so its n can be smaller than the markout's n; on that subset spread_capture_mean + mid_move_mean = markout_mean up to rounding, and a fill with no mid_before keeps its markout but is left out of the decomposition.

nodes.label: D-046 ReferenceBook::validate() sorts a copy to find duplicate ids
nodes.norm_label: d-046 referencebook::validate() sorts a copy to find duplicate ids
nodes.rationale: Same check as comparing every pair, but O(n log n) is fast enough to run twice per fuzz message.

nodes.label: DECISIONS.md
nodes.rationale: Decision log: one line per decision with the reason; section numbers refer to SPEC.md.

nodes.label: Avellaneda-Stoikov market maker (Phase 6; SPEC 1, 5.6 item 3, 9 item 6)
nodes.norm_label: avellaneda-stoikov market maker (phase 6; spec 1, 5.6 item 3, 9 item 6)

nodes.label: Matching engine API (Section 3 is silent on exact signatures)
nodes.norm_label: matching engine api (section 3 is silent on exact signatures)

nodes.label: D-010 Both books share one non-virtual member API
nodes.norm_label: d-010 both books share one non-virtual member api
nodes.rationale: submit, cancel, modify, best_bid, best_ask, best_level, depth, order, resting_orders and validate are the same on both books so tests are written once as typed tests over both; a virtual base would add an indirect call to the hot path for no benefit.

nodes.label: D-015 Platform-independent event hash encoding
nodes.rationale: One tag byte (Ack 0, Reject 1, Trade 2, Cancelled 3, Modified 4), then every field in declaration order, 64-bit fields as 8 bytes LE, 32-bit as 4 bytes LE, enums and bools as 1 byte: fixed and platform-independent (SPEC 3.7).

nodes.label: D-021 Cancel-reason precedence for market orders
nodes.norm_label: d-021 cancel-reason precedence for market orders
nodes.rationale: SelfTrade if STP CancelTaking stopped it (even with zero fills), else NoLiquidity if nothing filled, else IOCRemainder; a limit IOC remainder is always IOCRemainder, also with zero fills, because SPEC 3.3.3 reserves NoLiquidity for market orders.

nodes.label: D-022 Market order meeting only own CancelResting orders: NoLiquidity
nodes.norm_label: d-022 market order meeting only own cancelresting orders: noliquidity
nodes.rationale: Its only opposite liquidity was its own orders, cancelled under CancelResting, and nothing filled, so it ends with NoLiquidity.

nodes.label: D-023 Post-only would-cross is a pure price test
nodes.norm_label: d-023 post-only would-cross is a pure price test
nodes.rationale: SPEC 3.3.5 defines it by price only, so the test is against the opposite best whoever owns it.

nodes.label: D-024 Priority-losing modify re-enters as a GTC taker
nodes.norm_label: d-024 priority-losing modify re-enters as a gtc taker
nodes.rationale: SPEC 3.3.6 says it re-enters 'as a new arrival', so it uses the order's stored stp and post_only; under CancelTaking a self-match on re-entry cancels the re-entering order's remainder with Cancelled(SelfTrade).

nodes.label: D-027 Modify PostOnlyWouldCross check only for post-only orders
nodes.norm_label: d-027 modify postonlywouldcross check only for post-only orders
nodes.rationale: A normal order modified to a crossing price trades as a taker.

nodes.label: D-029 FOK only on limit orders; passed dry run always fills
nodes.norm_label: d-029 fok only on limit orders; passed dry run always fills
nodes.rationale: A market order must be IOC (SPEC 3.2), and execution walks the same orders the dry run counted, so a FOK that passes the dry run always fills completely.

nodes.label: D-030 Any taker stopped by CancelTaking gets Cancelled(SelfTrade)
nodes.norm_label: d-030 any taker stopped by canceltaking gets cancelled(selftrade)
nodes.rationale: SPEC 3.4 states it without exception, so D-021's 'limit IOC remainder is always IOCRemainder' applies only when STP did not stop it; a FOK can never end this way because it either fails the dry run or fills before reaching its own order (D-029).

nodes.label: D-093 At most one pending request per side
nodes.norm_label: d-093 at most one pending request per side
nodes.rationale: No new request is sent until the reply arrives (Ack/Reject(New) matched by client_order_id; Modified/Reject(Modify)/Cancelled(User)/Reject(Cancel) by kind and order id) and trades never clear a pending request. The requote runs after every BBO, every requote_interval wakeup and every private message; after a PostOnlyWouldCross reject it acts at once on a possibly stale BBO and resends until the fresh BBO arrives, with no extra back-off state.

nodes.label: D-096 Stress-test aggressor uses STP::CancelResting
nodes.rationale: With CancelTaking its market orders stopped at its own resting limits and the market maker was hit only 9 times in 30 s; with CancelResting a market order removes the aggressor's own orders in its way and reaches the quotes (about 4,800 market-maker fills per 60 s seed).

nodes.label: D-104 Window statistics integrated at every state change
nodes.norm_label: d-104 window statistics integrated at every state change
nodes.rationale: State is integrated over [max(warmup, previous event time), min(now, T)) at each request, fundamental step, sample and end, so the time-weighted spread distribution and quoting time are exact to the nanosecond with no sampling.

nodes.label: D-070 All simulator ties broken by the event queue's seq
nodes.norm_label: d-070 all simulator ties broken by the event queue's seq
nodes.rationale: Events with equal time run in scheduling order and event kind and agent id never take part; agents are created noise traders first, then the informed trader, then the market maker, so creation order fixes the seq of everything scheduled in on_start.

nodes.label: Array-ladder price index (SPEC Section 10 stretch goal)
nodes.norm_label: array-ladder price index (spec section 10 stretch goal)
nodes.rationale: An O(1) price index that would replace the O(log L) std::map lookup when adding an order to an existing price level.

nodes.label: Coordinated Omission
nodes.rationale: Closed-loop benchmarks underreport tail latency [18], so lobsim's benchmark numbers must be described as in-process closed-loop service time, not end-to-end latency under load.

nodes.label: lobsim_bench Throughput Harness
nodes.rationale: 10M seeded messages of noise-trader-like flow through OrderBook, reporting msgs/s and a per-message service-time histogram; ReferenceBook runs 100k messages for comparison. Release -O3 without sanitizers, printing CPU model, compiler and flags.

nodes.label: Order Node (intrusive doubly linked FIFO entry)
nodes.norm_label: order node (intrusive doubly linked fifo entry)

nodes.label: OrderBook (fast book)
nodes.rationale: Bids in std::map<Price, Level, std::greater<Price>>, asks in std::map<Price, Level>, begin() is the best price; std::map nodes have stable addresses so orders may point to their Level. Targets: cancel O(1) + level erase, add O(log L) for a new level and O(1) for an existing one.

nodes.label: Out-of-Scope Features
nodes.rationale: Multiple instruments, networking/FIX, multithreading, opening/closing auctions, stop/iceberg/hidden orders, decrement-and-cancel STP and real market data ingestion are not built but must be listed in the README.

nodes.label: Level (price, total_qty, count, head, tail)
nodes.rationale: Deleted as soon as it becomes empty.

nodes.rationale: What it is, an architecture diagram, the matching rules, design decisions and trade-offs, the benchmark table and a sample run (MM PnL, markouts, stylized facts) with an honest reading, plus what is not modeled and how to build, test and run.

nodes.rationale: Deliberately naive implementation of the identical interface and semantics: one std::vector of resting orders, best match by linear scan on (price, priority_seq), with priority_seq re-assigned when a modify loses priority. Readability over speed; it exists to catch bugs in OrderBook.

nodes.norm_label: stretch goals (array price ladder, lobster replay, rl wrapper)

nodes.rationale: Autonomous build spec for lobsim, a C++20 limit order book, matching engine and agent-based trading simulator, built in eight phases with acceptance checks. Bracketed citations explain why each rule exists; choices the spec leaves open go to DECISIONS.md.

nodes.norm_label: w. k. selph, how to build a fast limit order book
