nodes.label: D-050 Adding to an existing level is O(log L) via std::map
nodes.norm_label: d-050 adding to an existing level is o(log l) via std::map
nodes.rationale: SPEC 3.5 also fixes the level container as std::map, which has no O(1) lookup by price, and an incoming order carries no pointer to its level; only the best level is O(1) (begin()). L is tens of levels in the simulator, so this is a handful of comparisons.

nodes.label: Book Invariants (validate())
nodes.rationale: Run after every message in Debug and tests: the book is never crossed, each level's total_qty and count match its list, there are no empty levels or orders with remaining <= 0, and the id index points exactly at the resting orders.

nodes.label: Chunked Object Pool with Free List
nodes.norm_label: chunked object pool with free list
nodes.rationale: Orders must never live in a std::vector<Order> that can reallocate, because levels and the id index hold raw pointers that would dangle.

nodes.label: Correctness Before Speed
nodes.rationale: The simple ReferenceBook defines correct behaviour and the fast OrderBook must match it event for event.

nodes.label: Heap Allocation Counting (global operator new override)
nodes.norm_label: heap allocation counting (global operator new override)
nodes.rationale: Global operator new is overridden in the bench binary only; allocations are expected only when a new price level (std::map node) is created or a pool/vector grows, and the real number is reported.

nodes.label: Report Latency Distributions (percentiles + max)
nodes.rationale: Average latency hides the tail, so report p50/p90/p99/p99.9/max, never only the mean, and say what was measured (per-message service time).

nodes.label: Order Id Index (std::vector<Order*> indexed by OrderId)
nodes.norm_label: order id index (std::vector<order*> indexed by orderid)
nodes.rationale: Order ids are dense, so a vector index (set to nullptr on removal) avoids the per-insert hash-node allocations of std::unordered_map.

nodes.label: Phased Build with Acceptance Checks
nodes.rationale: Eight phases (skeleton, ReferenceBook, OrderBook, benchmarks, simulator core, informed trader + A–S MM, metrics/outputs/replay, README) are built in order; a phase is done only when its acceptance checks pass, the full Debug + sanitizer suite runs and is committed after each, and tests are never weakened to make them pass.

nodes.label: Price-Level Map + Intrusive FIFO Lists + Id Lookup
nodes.norm_label: price-level map + intrusive fifo lists + id lookup
nodes.rationale: O(1) cancel needs direct access to the order node; this is the classic fast LOB design of sorted price levels each holding a doubly linked FIFO list, plus a lookup from order id to order [1].

nodes.label: OrderBook internals and the differential fuzz test (Phase 3; Section 3.5 is silent on these)
nodes.norm_label: orderbook internals and the differential fuzz test (phase 3; section 3.5 is silent on these)

nodes.label: D-040 ObjectPool free list in a separate reserved vector
nodes.norm_label: d-040 objectpool free list in a separate reserved vector
nodes.rationale: A released slot is ASan-poisoned and must never be read, so free-list links cannot live inside free slots; the std::vector<void*> is reserved to the pool's full capacity whenever a chunk is added, so destroy() never allocates.

nodes.label: D-041 ObjectPool LIFO slot reuse in 4096-slot chunks
nodes.norm_label: d-041 objectpool lifo slot reuse in 4096-slot chunks
nodes.rationale: The most recently released slot is still in cache, and one chunk of 64-byte orders (256 KiB) covers a typical book without growing.

nodes.label: D-042 ObjectPool<T> requires trivially destructible T
nodes.norm_label: d-042 objectpool<t> requires trivially destructible t
nodes.rationale: The pool does not track which slots are live, so it cannot run destructors when it dies; enforced by static_assert, and Order is trivially destructible.

nodes.label: D-043 Priority-losing modify recycles the Order node
nodes.norm_label: d-043 priority-losing modify recycles the order node
nodes.rationale: The old Order node returns to the pool and a fresh one is taken if the remainder rests (same OrderId, same index slot): one removal path for cancel, fill and modify, and no node that is both resting and the taker during a match.

nodes.label: D-045 OrderBook is neither copyable nor movable
nodes.norm_label: d-045 orderbook is neither copyable nor movable
nodes.rationale: Orders point at map nodes and pool slots, so a copied book would alias the original's orders.

nodes.label: D-051 Deep-book differential test in order_book_validate_test
nodes.norm_label: d-051 deep-book differential test in order_book_validate_test
nodes.rationale: The fuzz test keeps the book under about 500 orders and never leaves the first pool chunk, so a separate test drives 8,500 resting orders across three pool chunks (scattered cancels, slot reuse, full drain) with an independent scan of the whole id index.

nodes.label: D-075 lobsim_run --duration-s override zeroes long warm-up
nodes.norm_label: d-075 lobsim_run --duration-s override zeroes long warm-up
nodes.rationale: If the shortened run is shorter than the configured warm-up, the warm-up is set to 0 instead of failing validation: a short run has no warm-up to keep.

nodes.label: D-076 Unknown, missing or mistyped config keys are errors
nodes.norm_label: d-076 unknown, missing or mistyped config keys are errors
nodes.rationale: A typo must not be silently ignored. The informed and mm sections are optional and are parsed and validated if present (Phase 5 created no agent for them, so runs with and without them were identical).

nodes.label: D-077 Config durations must fit 63 bits of nanoseconds
nodes.norm_label: d-077 config durations must fit 63 bits of nanoseconds
nodes.rationale: std::llround of a non-finite or out-of-range value is undefined behaviour, so such a duration is an error naming the field.

nodes.label: D-083 seconds_to_ns clamp and config duration bounds
nodes.norm_label: d-083 seconds_to_ns clamp and config duration bounds
nodes.rationale: Clamping a run-time draw to 4e18 ns (NaN included) and bounding duration_s to 1e9 s and every configured duration (latency, jitter, period) to 1e18 ns keeps now + draw below 2^63 for any valid run; before, a tiny lambda or a huge order_lifetime_mean_s could make the double-to-int64 cast undefined.

nodes.label: D-084 Config seed accepts any unsigned 64-bit value
nodes.norm_label: d-084 config seed accepts any unsigned 64-bit value
nodes.rationale: Same range as the --seed command-line option.

nodes.label: D-086 Informed trader threshold rule against the fundamental
nodes.norm_label: d-086 informed trader threshold rule against the fundamental
nodes.rationale: Buy if V - ask >= theta (needs an ask in the local BBO), else sell if bid - V >= theta (needs a bid), compared in ticks as doubles; a one-sided BBO evaluates only the side it has and the buy wins if both hold (impossible with a non-crossed book and theta >= 0). Orders are market IOC with STP::CancelTaking and an own client_order_id counter from 1; nothing rests, so on_private only counts events.

nodes.label: D-085 Informed trader's single price-independent wakeup chain
nodes.norm_label: d-085 informed trader's single price-independent wakeup chain
nodes.rationale: on_start and every on_wakeup draw exactly one exponential from ctx.rng() and schedule the next wakeup before looking at the market, so its wakeup times never depend on prices; it reads only the last BBO it received and Fundamental::value() at wakeup, and uses plain schedule_wakeup (no TimerQueue) because it has a single kind of timer.

nodes.label: D-014 validate() throws std::logic_error; Debug runs it per message
nodes.norm_label: d-014 validate() throws std::logic_error; debug runs it per message
nodes.rationale: validate() names the first broken invariant; a thrown error is testable and gives a message, an assert does neither.

nodes.label: D-080 Exchange throws if the book is ever crossed
nodes.norm_label: d-080 exchange throws if the book is ever crossed
nodes.rationale: A crossed book after a request can only mean an engine bug, so std::logic_error is thrown in every build type.

nodes.label: D-108 Request and order counts by type and role
nodes.norm_label: d-108 request and order counts by type and role
nodes.rationale: Requests by type are those arriving at the exchange (they sum to Exchange::requests()); 'orders sent' per role counts NewOrder sends by agents (some may still be in flight at T); roles follow creation order (noise traders, informed trader, market maker), and agents added by tests are Role::Other and not reported.

nodes.label: Book Query API (best_bid, best_ask, depth, order)
nodes.norm_label: book query api (best_bid, best_ask, depth, order)

nodes.label: D-013 best_level(side) returns best price and quantity, no allocation
nodes.norm_label: d-013 best_level(side) returns best price and quantity, no allocation
nodes.rationale: The exchange needs BBO quantities after every message, and depth() returns a vector.

nodes.label: A–S Total Spread δ = γσ²(T−t) + (2/γ)ln(1+γ/κ)
nodes.rationale: Quotes sit symmetrically around the reservation price: bid = r − δ/2, ask = r + δ/2.

nodes.label: D-091 Quotes from one pure function compute_quotes()
nodes.norm_label: d-091 quotes from one pure function compute_quotes()
nodes.rationale: A pure function is tested on its own; tau = max(0, end - now) in seconds; prices stay doubles until the range check so an extreme r never overflows the integer conversion; 'ensure bid < ask' lowers the bid to ask - 1, reachable (with delta > 0 and the two clamps) only when r +- delta/2 rounds onto the same integer.

nodes.label: Inventory control fading near session end
nodes.norm_label: inventory control fading near session end
nodes.rationale: Observed in the chart: after the 60 s warm-up the inventory mean-reverts tightly around zero (within roughly +/-5-7 lots) until about 2200 s, widens to about +/-10 lots by 3000 s and +/-15-20 lots by 3400 s, then swings violently in the final minutes, peaking near +51 lots at about 3560 s and closing deeply short (roughly -35 lots) at 3600 s. Why: the market maker quotes with finite-horizon Avellaneda-Stoikov. reservation_price() shifts the quotes against inventory by gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) ticks per lot, and compute_quotes() sets tau = end - now, which reaches 0 at the session end (0.36 ticks per lot at the start with the default gamma=0.0001, sigma=1, T=3600 s; about 0.03 with 5 minutes left). As the skew vanishes the quotes become nearly symmetric around the mid, so fills are no longer pushed back toward flat and inventory random-walks with the order flow, bounded only by the q_max=50 cutoff (no bid at +50 or more, no ask at -50 or less), which is why the peak sits just past 50.

nodes.label: MM Quote Rounding and Clamping
nodes.rationale: bid = floor(r − δ/2), ask = ceil(r + δ/2), clamped so bid <= local best ask − 1 and ask >= local best bid + 1 with bid < ask. Per side: no working order gives NewOrder, a different price gives Modify, a side that should not be quoted gives Cancel.

nodes.label: D-105 Time-weighted spread quantiles and 1-40 tick histogram
nodes.norm_label: d-105 time-weighted spread quantiles and 1-40 tick histogram
nodes.rationale: Median, p90 and p99 are the smallest integer spread whose cumulative time reaches p * total; the histogram has one bin per spread of 1..40 ticks (fraction of two-sided time) plus an overflow bin, and a spread of 0 cannot exist because the book is never crossed.

nodes.label: Differential fuzz test (fuzz_diff)
nodes.rationale: 200 seeds x 10,000 random valid and invalid requests (--long for 4 x 1,000,000); both books must produce identical events, queries and hashes; fails if any event type, reject reason, cancel reason or self-trade path never occurred.

nodes.label: lob_tests unit tests
nodes.rationale: Every matching rule as small hand-checked scenarios, typed over both books, with validate() and a quantity-conservation checker after every message.

nodes.label: lobsim_bench throughput harness
nodes.rationale: 10M seeded messages shaped like noise-trader flow, generation outside every timed region; replaces global operator new to count engine allocations.

nodes.label: micro_bench microbenchmarks
nodes.rationale: Books pre-filled to 1,000 and 100,000 orders; batches of 128 undone outside the timed region; calibration benchmarks show the timer pause adds 3.4 to 4.0 ns per operation.

nodes.label: ObjectPool
nodes.rationale: Chunked pool (4,096 orders per chunk) with a free list so order addresses never move; a released slot is poisoned under AddressSanitizer.

nodes.label: Order-id index (std::vector<Order*>)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over std::unordered_map: no allocation per order, O(1) cancel, stable addresses. Cost: memory proportional to the highest order id and a large copy when the vector doubles, which is the benchmark's maximum latency; reserving the index removes it.

nodes.label: OrderBook
nodes.rationale: Fast book: std::map<Price, Level> with opposite comparators so begin() is the best price, intrusive FIFO per level, pooled orders with stable addresses, id-indexed vector for O(1) lookup; about 47.5M msgs/s, 31x ReferenceBook.

nodes.label: ReferenceBook
nodes.rationale: Deliberately naive vector with linear scans, written to be read and checked against the specification; shares only the type and event headers with OrderBook.

nodes.label: validate() invariant checker
nodes.rationale: Checks book not crossed, level totals and counts, list links, id index pointing exactly at resting orders, pool count; runs after every message in debug builds and tests.

nodes.label: Coordinated omission
nodes.rationale: Closed-loop in-process service times hide queueing delay, so tail latency in a real system would be worse than the tails shown.

nodes.label: Heap allocation audit
nodes.rationale: 0.0130 allocations per message; allocations happen only when a price level is created or when the pool or a vector grows, as the design predicts.

nodes.label: Intrusive doubly linked FIFO per price level
nodes.norm_label: intrusive doubly linked fifo per price level

nodes.label: steady_clock 41 ns timer step
nodes.rationale: Too coarse for single ~21 ns messages: use the block-timed row for the mean, batch-of-32 for the body, per-message samples only for the far tail.

nodes.label: Price-time priority matching
nodes.rationale: Best price first, earliest order first within a level; every trade prints at the resting maker's price; GTC remainder rests at the level tail, IOC or market remainder is cancelled.

nodes.label: Two books, one behaviour
nodes.rationale: A readable ReferenceBook and a fast OrderBook share only type and event headers; unit tests run against both and the fuzz test requires identical events.

nodes.label: D-088 noise_traders.reference_price: floor or symmetric
nodes.rationale: floor is the SPEC 5.6 rule (buy at floor(mid) - d, sell at floor(mid) + d); symmetric buys at ceil(mid) - d and sells at floor(mid) + d, differing only when the local BBO is two-sided with an odd spread, needing no random draw and leaving the fallbacks (last trade, initial price) unchanged. Any other value is an error naming the field; to_json always writes it.

nodes.label: D-089 Default config uses the symmetric reference price
nodes.norm_label: d-089 default config uses the symmetric reference price
nodes.rationale: The one deliberate departure from the SPEC 5.8 values: under the floor rule an odd spread lets sell limits (ref + d) improve the best ask by a tick while buy limits (ref - d) can only join the best bid. Over 12 seeds of a noise-only one-hour run the final mid minus the start price was -91 to -117 ticks with floor, +97 to +121 with the mid rounded up and -9 to +15 with symmetric: a rounding artefact larger than the fundamental's one-hour standard deviation (60 ticks).

nodes.label: D-090 reference_price optional, defaults to floor
nodes.norm_label: d-090 reference_price optional, defaults to floor
nodes.rationale: The JSON of SPEC 5.8 keeps meaning exactly what the spec says and simtest::default_json() stays the spec text; the noise-only one-hour hash ac6dbb79a513fa50 is unchanged.

nodes.label: D-094 Messages that fit no state count in anomalies()
nodes.norm_label: d-094 messages that fit no state count in anomalies()
nodes.rationale: They never crash or corrupt state: an unmatched reply is ignored; a trade for an unknown order still moves the inventory (it happened); a Cancelled other than the reply to a pending cancel removes the order; Reject(UnknownOrder) for an order believed resting drops it; Modified for an order believed gone takes the exchange's word. In a correct run the counter is 0 and the tests assert it.

nodes.label: Own Distributions (uniform int, uniform [0,1), exponential, Box–Muller normal)
nodes.norm_label: own distributions (uniform int, uniform [0,1), exponential, box–muller normal)
nodes.rationale: Uniform int uses rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias; exponential is −ln(1−u)/λ; normal uses Box–Muller.

nodes.label: D-082 Rejection-sampling bias test on a 3 * 2^62 range
nodes.norm_label: d-082 rejection-sampling bias test on a 3 * 2^62 range
nodes.rationale: The modulo bias on a range of 3 values is about 2^-64 and cannot be measured, whereas on this range the lowest third would have probability 1/2 instead of 1/3 without rejection.

nodes.label: Market-maker inventory, sampled (seed 42)
nodes.rationale: Chart of the market maker's inventory (lots) against simulated time (0-3600 s, one hour) for the default-config seed-42 sample run. It is drawn as a post-step line because inventory is piecewise-constant between the one-second ground-truth samples. The grey band marks the 60 s warm-up that the metrics exclude, and the black zero line is the flat-inventory level that the quotes' inventory skew pulls toward.

nodes.label: D-081 One latency generator per agent, per-channel FIFO clamp
nodes.norm_label: d-081 one latency generator per agent, per-channel fifo clamp
nodes.rationale: One generator is shared by the entry, response and feed channels and drawn when a message is scheduled; each channel keeps FIFO order with max(sampled, last arrival on the channel).

nodes.label: Warm-up window (shaded)
nodes.rationale: Grey band from t=0 to about 60 s (config warmup_s). It marks the start-up period so the reader can discount it; the plot tool computes its statistics only from the time after the warm-up.

nodes.label: Seed-42 sample run
nodes.rationale: The chart's data source: one simulator run with seed 42 (named in the title) over one simulated hour (x-axis to ~3,600 s), the README's default-config sample run. 'Sampled' in the title means each point is a periodic sample of the PnL (every sample_interval_s, 1 s in the default config), not a value recorded at every fill, so moves between samples are not shown.

nodes.label: D-001 CMake from a project-local uv venv
nodes.norm_label: d-001 cmake from a project-local uv venv
nodes.rationale: The machine had no CMake, and a project-local .venv (uv pip install cmake) changes nothing outside the repo; the same venv holds pandas and matplotlib for tools/plot.py.

nodes.label: D-111 tools/plot.py uses the sampled bbo.csv rows
nodes.norm_label: d-111 tools/plot.py uses the sampled bbo.csv rows
nodes.rationale: It needs only pandas, matplotlib and numpy, draws the warm-up as a grey band, and takes the spread histogram and return ACF from the sampled bbo.csv rows, so its numbers are the sampled ones rather than the time-weighted ones of summary.json; it exits 1 with a message if bbo.csv or summary.json is missing.

nodes.label: D-073 One TimerQueue entry per schedule_wakeup; pop_due throws
nodes.norm_label: d-073 one timerqueue entry per schedule_wakeup; pop_due throws
nodes.rationale: Each on_wakeup pops exactly one entry and pop_due throws if none is due: a lost or duplicate wakeup is an error and timers add no second tie rule; timers are never erased, so an obsolete cancel timer is popped and ignored.

nodes.label: D-064 Benchmark harness fails on pass, id or hash mismatch
nodes.norm_label: d-064 benchmark harness fails on pass, id or hash mismatch
nodes.rationale: A benchmark of a broken run is worse than none. Passes are compared on event counts, not a full event hash, because hashing inside the block-timed loop would add its own cost to the measured time; the full hash is computed in the per-message pass, outside its timer pairs, and compared with ReferenceBook.

nodes.label: D-071 RNG streams seeded by (seed, role, index, purpose)
nodes.norm_label: d-071 rng streams seeded by (seed, role, index, purpose)
nodes.rationale: Never seeded from the global agent index, so adding a noise trader, the informed trader or the market maker leaves every other stream unchanged (tested by comparing the NewOrder lines of N and N+1 traders).

nodes.label: D-092 Reprice by Modify only when an extra quote fits q_max
nodes.norm_label: d-092 reprice by modify only when an extra quote fits q_max
nodes.rationale: A Modify resets the remaining quantity, so one arriving after unseen fills refills the order: always modifying allows |q| up to q_max + 2 * quote_size - 2, while this rule bounds |q| by q_max + quote_size - 1 (argument in as_market_maker.cpp). Otherwise the order is cancelled and the NewOrder comes from the ordinary requote once the cancel's reply has arrived; the stress test reaches exactly 14 with q_max 10 and quote_size 5.

nodes.label: D-095 Market maker: no random draws, one wakeup chain
nodes.norm_label: d-095 market maker: no random draws, one wakeup chain
nodes.rationale: on_start schedules requote_interval and each on_wakeup schedules the next one, then requotes, with plain schedule_wakeup like the informed trader (D-085). It is created last with streams (MarketMaker, 0) and Simulator::market_maker_index() returns its index; lobsim_run prints its true inventory, maximum |q| and fills from an observer over engine Trade events, and its requests, rejects and anomalies from the agent's own counters.

nodes.label: Adverse Selection
nodes.rationale: Maker quotes tend to be filled exactly when the price is about to move against the maker; lobsim creates it deliberately with an informed trader and measures it with markouts instead of assuming it away.

nodes.label: AvellanedaStoikovMM Agent
nodes.rationale: Quotes one post-only GTC bid and ask of quote_size, recomputed on every BBO update and every requote_interval from its local mid, its own-fill inventory, config σ (ticks per √s) and T = duration_s. The simulation ends at T and final PnL marks the remaining inventory to the exchange's last mid.

nodes.label: Market Making
nodes.rationale: A market maker quotes both sides to earn the spread but carries inventory risk and suffers adverse selection.

nodes.label: Markouts
nodes.rationale: For each MM fill at time t and horizon h: buy m(t+h) − p, sell p − m(t+h), per lot in ticks with m the exchange mid; mean and 95% CI per horizon, skipping and counting samples where the mid is undefined. The CI assumes independent fills, which overlapping horizons violate (stated in the README). Negative markouts mean adverse selection.

nodes.label: A–S Reservation Price r = s − qγσ²(T−t)
nodes.norm_label: a–s reservation price r = s − qγσ2(t−t)
nodes.rationale: Shifts both quotes against inventory (long means quote lower to sell), pushing the maker back toward a flat position.

nodes.label: Avellaneda & Stoikov (2008), via Hummingbot's Technical Deep Dive
nodes.norm_label: avellaneda & stoikov (2008), via hummingbot's technical deep dive

nodes.label: Lalor & Swishchuk, Market Simulation under Adverse Selection
nodes.norm_label: lalor & swishchuk, market simulation under adverse selection

nodes.label: Market Making under a Weakly Consistent Limit Order Book Model
nodes.norm_label: market making under a weakly consistent limit order book model
nodes.rationale: Cited for LOB models with unrealistic price dynamics overstating mean MM profit by about 50-60%.

nodes.label: The Negative Drift of a Limit Order Fill
nodes.norm_label: the negative drift of a limit order fill

nodes.label: Inventory Limit Q_max
nodes.rationale: No bid when q >= Q_max and no ask when q <= −Q_max; with one resting order per side, |q| <= Q_max + quote_size holds at all times (at most one quote's overshoot), a phase-6 acceptance check.

nodes.label: No Assumed Fills (informed trader + markouts)
nodes.rationale: Optimistic fill models invent profit: assuming limit orders fill with probability 1 produces backtests that look profitable but fail [11], and LOB models with unrealistic price dynamics overstated mean MM profit by about 50-60% [12]. So fills are never assumed, an informed trader creates adverse selection, and markouts are reported.

nodes.label: EventQueue
nodes.rationale: Min-heap on (time_ns, seq); simulation time is int64 nanoseconds with no wall-clock time.

nodes.label: Exchange
nodes.rationale: Processes a request the instant it arrives, sends private events to their owners, broadcasts TradePrint per trade and BBO on any top-of-book change, and appends every arriving request to orders.log.

nodes.label: InformedTrader
nodes.rationale: Poisson 2/s; market buy or sell of 5 lots when the fundamental value is at least 2 ticks beyond its view of the ask or bid.

nodes.label: NoiseTrader
nodes.rationale: Ten zero-intelligence traders at Poisson 5/s: 85% limit orders 1-10 ticks from their view of the mid, 15% market, sizes 1-10 lots, each resting order cancelled after an exponential lifetime with mean 30 s.

nodes.label: Order-log codec
nodes.rationale: One codec for orders.log used by both the exchange and the replay tool; the replay test goes through the text.

nodes.label: Fundamental value V
nodes.rationale: Driftless random walk, 1 tick per square-root second, stepped every 0.1 s; read only by the informed trader. The mid follows it only loosely (mean gap 8.5 ticks).

nodes.label: Latency channels (entry, response, feed)
nodes.rationale: Each a constant plus uniform jitter; a channel is FIFO so a message never arrives before an earlier message on the same channel.

nodes.label: sim (discrete-event simulator)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and single-threaded; agents see the market only through delayed messages and fills happen only through the engine, so queue position is real.

nodes.label: Custom RNG distributions
nodes.rationale: Own uniform-integer (rejection sampling, no modulo bias), uniform, exponential and normal (Box-Muller) distributions, because std:: distributions differ between standard libraries.

nodes.label: D-107 Mid sampling and return statistics
nodes.norm_label: d-107 mid sampling and return statistics
nodes.rationale: The mid is sampled at k * sample_interval for warmup <= k * interval <= T (the sample at T taken at the end), each sample seeing the state after every event ordered before the kernel's Sample event (time, then seq), and bbo.csv also has the t = 0 row. A log return exists only between two consecutive present samples; excess kurtosis is m4 / m2^2 - 3 with central moments divided by n; autocorrelation uses pairs where both terms exist, around the mean of all present values, with nothing interpolated. Returns of a half-tick-quantised mid are mostly zero or one of a few tick-sized values.

nodes.label: D-103 Market-maker resting orders tracked from engine events
nodes.norm_label: d-103 market-maker resting orders tracked from engine events
nodes.rationale: Tracked from the Ack of its own NewOrder, Trade, Cancelled and Modified rather than read from the book; 'quoting' means at least one resting bid and one resting ask, and the quoted spread is its lowest ask minus its highest bid.

nodes.label: MetricsObserver
nodes.rationale: Computes metrics from ground truth (engine events and the true book), never from an agent's beliefs, after the 60 s warm-up.

nodes.label: tools/sweep.py
nodes.rationale: Runs 89 one-hour simulations (about 30 s) and prints the four multi-seed tables used in the README; needs only the standard library.

nodes.label: Adverse selection
nodes.rationale: Hidden by positive aggregate markouts: a mechanical half-tick mid move plus a mix of counterparties; fills against the informed trader lose -0.68 ticks per lot at 30 s by default, -2.5 to -2.9 with a stronger informed trader.

nodes.label: Bid-ask bounce
nodes.rationale: Explains lag-1 return autocorrelation of -0.24 to -0.37: the mid lives on a half-tick grid with a 1-to-3-tick spread.

nodes.label: Informed-trader variant sweep
nodes.rationale: Adverse selection shows as lower PnL per lot (0.497 with no informed trader, 0.384 with the strongest); total PnL does not fall because informed orders add volume.

nodes.label: Markouts (spread capture + mid move)
nodes.rationale: m(t+h) - p for a buy, split into spread capture against the pre-trade mid and the later mid move; 95% intervals assume independent fills, so they are likely too narrow.

nodes.label: Stylized facts analysis
nodes.rationale: Heavy tails only weakly present, lag-1 return autocorrelation strongly negative, no slowly decaying volatility clustering.

nodes.label: Zero-intelligence order flow
nodes.rationale: Chosen as a simple, explainable baseline; it reproduces bid-ask bounce but not fat tails or long-memory volatility, and the simulator does not tune anything to fake them. It is also why the market maker profits.

nodes.label: D-048 ConservationChecker::check_fast() in O(open + touched)
nodes.rationale: It gives check()'s verdict by comparing the book's resting_orders() with the model's live count instead of re-querying every finished id; the fuzz test runs it on every message and runs check() beside it on every 20th seed (verdicts must agree), and --long uses check_fast() only because check() is quadratic over 10^6 messages.

nodes.label: D-047 Fuzz generator: SplitMix64 with rejection-sampled ranges
nodes.norm_label: d-047 fuzz generator: splitmix64 with rejection-sampled ranges
nodes.rationale: It never draws two random values inside one function-call argument list (unspecified evaluation order), so the same seed gives the same stream on any compiler.

nodes.label: D-072 Message-triggered draws use a separate per-agent stream
nodes.norm_label: d-072 message-triggered draws use a separate per-agent stream
nodes.rationale: ctx.rng() is drawn only in on_start and on_wakeup. Whether a reply is handled before or after the agent's next wakeup depends on latency jitter, consumed at a rate set by every other agent, so sharing the decision stream would re-phase it when an agent is added; the noise trader draws each order lifetime on the Ack of a limit order from its own lifetime stream (purpose 2).

nodes.label: D-079 Simulator::add_agent for scripted test agents
nodes.norm_label: d-079 simulator::add_agent for scripted test agents
nodes.rationale: Tests add scripted agents after the configured ones; they take their streams from StreamRole::Test (or any role and index the test gives) and are indexed after the configured agents.

nodes.label: Accelerating market-maker PnL growth
nodes.rationale: Read off the chart: PnL rises almost monotonically from 0 to about +12,300 ticks at 3,600 s, with no drawdown larger than a few tens of ticks. The slope steepens over the hour: about 1.4 ticks/s in the first 1,000 s (+1,400 at 1,000 s), 3.7 in the second 1,000 s (+5,100 at 2,000 s), 4.2 in the third (+9,300 at 3,000 s) and about 5 in the last 600 s. The two halves of the post-warm-up window gain about +4,260 and +7,960, matching the README's +4,291 and +7,973 (+12,263 after warm-up). The README's untested explanation: early in the session the Avellaneda-Stoikov inventory term gamma*sigma^2*(T-t) in the reservation price is large (0.36 ticks per lot), so after a fill the market maker quotes near the mid to unload and earns less per lot; later its quotes stay symmetric and it earns about a full tick per lot while carrying more inventory.

nodes.label: Mark-to-market PnL (ticks)
nodes.rationale: Y-axis metric: market-maker cash plus inventory valued at the last exchange mid, minus fees, in ticks (MetricsObserver::pnl_now), recorded at every sample time into the mm_pnl column of bbo.csv. Because inventory is valued at the mid, the curve includes unrealized gains and losses on open inventory, not only realized spread capture.

nodes.label: Warm-up window (0-60 s)
nodes.rationale: The grey band over 0-60 s is the warm-up (SimConfig warmup_s, 60 s in configs/default.json), drawn by shade_warmup in tools/plot.py. Statistics use only the time after it, so the start-up transient stays out of the reported figures: the reported PnL after warm-up subtracts the PnL at 60 s (about +40 ticks here), while the plotted curve itself is cumulative from t = 0.

nodes.label: Market-maker PnL, sampled (seed 42)
nodes.rationale: Sample-run figure written by tools/plot.py and embedded in the README's market-maker results: one line of the market maker's mark-to-market PnL in ticks against simulated time (0 to ~3,600 s), a black zero line, and a grey band over the first 60 s marking the warm-up. It shows how the market maker's PnL builds up over the session, not just the end-of-run total.

nodes.label: D-101 Metric state: after all events with timestamp <= t
nodes.norm_label: d-101 metric state: after all events with timestamp <= t
nodes.rationale: For the warm-up instant the state is after all events with timestamp < warmup, so the window [warmup, T] is closed at its start and pnl_after_warmup = pnl(T) - pnl(warmup) counts exactly the fills with t >= warmup; events at exactly T are never processed (kernel rule), so the final state is the state at T.

nodes.label: Negative Lag-1 Return Autocorrelation (about -0.35)
nodes.rationale: Lag 1 is about -0.35 and lag 2 about -0.07, both far outside the ±0.033 band, so a move tends to be partly undone over the next one or two samples. That is the usual signature of microstructure noise such as bid-ask bounce, or a mid-price that flickers while a depleted quote refills. The plot does not say whether these are trade-price or mid-price returns, so the mechanism is an interpretation.

nodes.label: No Significant Return Autocorrelation Beyond Lag 2
nodes.norm_label: no significant return autocorrelation beyond lag 2
nodes.rationale: From lag 3 to lag 20 the bars stay inside the band except lag 12 (about +0.03, at the edge) and lag 13 (about -0.04). That is close to the one exceedance expected by chance over 18 lags at 5%, so past returns carry little linear information about returns more than two samples ahead.

nodes.label: Seed 42 Run
nodes.rationale: Fixing the seed makes the run behind this plot reproducible. Both panels use the same 3540 return observations left after the warm-up is dropped.

nodes.label: ±1.96/√n Significance Band
nodes.rationale: Under a white-noise null each sample autocorrelation is roughly N(0, 1/n), so ±1.96/√n is a pointwise 95% band; with n = 3540 it is about ±0.033. A single bar outside it is significant at 5%, and over 20 lags about one chance exceedance is expected.

nodes.label: Stylized Facts of Asset Returns
nodes.rationale: Plotting the ACF of returns beside the ACF of absolute returns is the standard check of two stylized facts: little linear autocorrelation beyond the shortest lags, and slowly decaying positive autocorrelation of absolute returns (volatility clustering).

nodes.label: Volatility Clustering
nodes.rationale: The ACF of absolute returns is significantly positive at lags 1-5 (about 0.16, 0.10, 0.06, 0.06, 0.05) and inside the band from lag 6, so large moves tend to follow large moves. Within the 20 lags shown the effect fades after about five samples rather than decaying slowly. Some of the lag-1 value may come from the reversals themselves, since a move and its reversal have similar size.

nodes.label: Warm-up Period
nodes.rationale: Only data from after the warm-up enters the plot, presumably so the start-up transient does not bias the autocorrelations. The plot does not show how long the warm-up is.
